title: Background spectra cut cross-site wave-power variation by 75% in eight Hawaii tsunami-report events, 2015-2025
abstract: We tested whether coastal background spectra can remove site effects from post-earthquake wave spectra. We reused fixed six-minute records from six Hawaii gauges for 22 earthquakes in 2015-2026. Each target used a station background template from other earthquakes only. In eight events with Hawaii tsunami reports, the template reduced cross-site log-power variance at periods of 24-120 minutes by 74.8% (conditional 95% earthquake-bootstrap interval 64.2-83.0%). All eight improved. Four strong-growth events gave 73.7%. A template fixed from 2015-2020 reduced variance by 81.2% in the three later reported events. The correct station labels ranked first among all 720 template assignments. Direct FFT calculations reproduced the Welch spectra. After correction, reported-event spectra still had 2.55 times the cross-site variance of their prior-day controls. These results support a transferable site component at these gauges. They do not identify a unique coastal response or predict absolute waves. This applies an established spectral-ratio method with held-out events; it is not a new spectral method. Few tsunami events, background power, six-minute sampling, shared template error and origin-based windows limit the result. External records remain outside the bundle; code, exact source locators and hashes, aggregate results and a figure are included.

display.caption: Cross-site log-power variance before and after a station background template from other events. Intervals resample earthquakes and hold the templates fixed. Strong events are a subgroup of reported events.
